good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the rst policy with insurer
good.reference: Section IV (Conditions) > Standard Exclusions > 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code Excl 01 (page 3-4 of provided extract)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are not covered for the first 36 months from the policy start date. Claims for PEDs will be payable only after completing 3 years of continuous coverage.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the rst policy with us.
good.reference: Section IV (Conditions) > Standard Exclusions > 2. Specied disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02 (page 3-4 of provided extract)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months from the policy start date. You can claim for these only after completing 2 years of continuous coverage.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the rst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Section IV (Conditions) > Standard Exclusions > 3. 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03 (page 3-4 of provided extract)
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days, but accident claims are covered immediately. Plan purchases should be done before you anticipate non-accident treatment.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room, boarding, nursing expenses (all inclusive) as provided by the Hospital / Nursing Home up to  Rs.5,000/- per day
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > A (page 2 of provided extract)
bad.explanation: Room rent (including boarding and nursing) is capped at 5,000 per day. Staying in a higher-priced room can lead to reduced claim payout and higher out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: Expenses relating to hospitalization will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent stated in the policy or actual whichever is less
bad.explanation: Hospitalization expenses are paid in proportion to the eligible room rent limit or actual room rent, whichever is less. If you choose a room above the 5,000/day cap, many other bills can be reduced proportionately.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: This policy is subject to co-payment of 20% of each and every claim amount for fresh as well as renewal policies
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > G. Co-payment (page 2 of provided extract)
bad.explanation: A mandatory co-pay of 20% applies on each and every claim for both fresh and renewal policies. You will always bear 20% of admissible expenses, which can significantly increase your out-of-pocket share.

bad.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
bad.quote: Post Hospitalization expenses: A sum equivalent to 7% of the hospitalization expenses or actuals incurred up to 60 days after discharge from the hospital following an admissible claim whichever is higher
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > E (page 2 of provided extract)
bad.explanation: Post-hospitalization expenses are covered up to 60 days after discharge, limited to 7% of hospitalization expenses or actuals, whichever is higher. Follow-up medicines/tests beyond these limits may not be reimbursed.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Sublimits: The expenses incurred on treatment of the following procedure are payable up-to the limits mentioned hereunder;
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > F. Sublimits (page 2 of provided extract)
bad.explanation: Certain procedures are payable only up to the sub-limits mentioned in the table. Even if your sum insured is higher, payouts for those treatments can be capped.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern Treatments The expenses payable during the entire policy period for the following treatment / procedure ... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below;
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > H. Coverage for Modern Treatments (page 2 of provided extract)
bad.explanation: Modern treatments are covered but limited to the amounts shown in the table for the entire policy period. If the actual cost is higher than the sub-limit, you will pay the difference.

bad.name: Ambulance Cover
bad.quote: Emergency ambulance charges, actual subject to a maximum of Rs.750/- per hospitalization and overall limit of Rs.1,500/- per policy period
bad.reference: Section II (Coverage) > D (page 2 of provided extract)
bad.explanation: Emergency ambulance is covered up to 750 per hospitalization with an overall cap of 1,500 per policy period. Any ambulance cost above these limits will be out of pocket.
